items.detail: The tail of the wet season, so expect a grey day or two and keep the hardshell reachable. Mornings near 10 °C, afternoons near 20 °C — one layer over a shirt covers the whole day. The 400 m does nothing to you: this is the only leg where the weather is unremarkable, which makes it the right place to buy what you did not fly in.

Heated and sealed, and oxygen-enriched above Golmud, so the cabin holds around 20 °C the whole way even as the line crosses Tanggula at 5,072 m. What bites is the dryness and the glass: hours of full high-altitude sun through a window. The platform stops at Xining and Golmud are genuinely cold — keep a fleece by the berth, not in the bag overhead.

October is the dry season and the clearest month of the year, which is why the tour runs now. The swing is the story, not the cold: 20 °C in direct sun at midday, 5 °C or below within an hour of it setting. Almost no rain, very low humidity, and UV strong enough to burn in an hour. Layers you shed at 11:00 and put back on at 17:00.

The one night that needs real kit. Around 10 °C in sun, about −6 °C overnight, and wind off the glacier makes it feel far colder than that. Clear skies are likely — that is the point of October — and clear skies are exactly why it drops so hard after dark. You sleep in base layers, hat and heavy socks, inside a rented bag under the camp quilts.

Back to sea level and back to humidity: 22 °C days, 15 °C nights, and the tail of typhoon season, so a wet afternoon is plausible. After a week on the plateau it will feel warm and heavy rather than mild. The park days share exactly one problem with Tibet — twelve hours of unbroken sun — so the hat and the sunscreen keep earning their place.
